thread:
incident-bot: P0 alert: Smart-routing anomalies detected for tenant 'acme-corp' — high error spike and unexpected spillover from dedicated pool to hosted. Automatically opened incident thread. Paging alex_m (oncall).

alex_m (oncall): on it. seeing 502/timeout surge and a bunch of requests routed to hosted-ff-prod-1 that should have stayed in dedicated-acme-1. Isolation flag cleared?

maya (eng-sre): jumping in. initial quick check: routing-policy service reports fallback decisions for acme-corp going to hosted tier instead of preferred dedicated variant. Looks like a policy evaluation return path looped to region fallback -> hosted.

sam (runtime): logs show KV-cache warm misses and model-variant selection logs: model_variant="gptx-8q" expected pool=dedicated-acme-1 but assigned_pool=hosted-ff-prod-1. Routing decision path: capacity-tier -> region-fallback -> model-compat-check -> assign. The region-fallback returned a list with hosted before dedicated due to a stale priority list in config.

alex_m (oncall): quoting deploy-bot: "config-change by infra-ci 2123448800: routing/policies/acme-corp.yaml updated" — could be the culprit. @maya @sam can we roll back that policy?

maya (eng-sre): I can roll it back. snapshot shows change: fallback_order was accidentally edited to include 'hosted' for 'preferred' fallback due to a templating bug. Patch diff:

```
- fallback_order: [regional, hosted]
+ fallback_order: [regional, dedicated, hosted]
```

That explains why requests fell through to hosted when dedicated had transient capacity hiccup. The templating generator omitted 'dedicated' for some tenants when a feature flag was false.

sam (runtime): mitigation plan: 1) push config rollback to routing service (hot reload) 2) add immediate route override for acme-corp -> dedicated-acme-1 3) quarantine hosted pool routing for acme-corp to prevent any more writes there.

alex_m (oncall): do it. mark as page-to-pager for any further regression.

maya (eng-sre): rolling back now. applying previous revision: routing/policies/acme-corp.yaml@2123444400 -> deploying to config-service. hot-reload request sent.

devops-bot: deploy started by maya. Deployment id: cfg-98765. Target: routing-policy-service (canary -> global).

sam (runtime): applying route override:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.routing/v1/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","target_pool":"dedicated-acme-1","ttl_seconds":3600}'
```
Override applied. Also put host-filter rule: deny routing to hosted-ff-prod-1 for tenant acme-corp.

tina (customer-svcs): heads-up — acme-corp support reported increased 5xx from their integrations ~about 20 minutes ago. Customer success on the line. Any ETA for full recovery? They are watching SLAs.

maya (eng-sre): config rollback completed, canary passed, propagating globally. I see routing decision metrics normalizing. Error rate for acme-corp dropping from 9% -> 1.2% in last 3 mins.

sam (runtime): KV-cache warm-ups finishing. latency returning to baseline. Hosted pool had partial handling but some requests got lower-quality variants — need to check output regressions.

alex_m (oncall): marking incident state: mitigation in place. Paging customer-svcs to update acme. Setting priority to P0 until validated for 30 minutes.

maya (eng-sre): root cause notes so far: templating feature-flag path omitted 'dedicated' in fallback_order for a small set of tenants during a config regen pipeline job (infra-ci). When dedicated had transient capacity signals (autoscaler pressure/short eviction), the fallback evaluation fell into hosted path earlier than intended. That produced isolation breach: tenant traffic briefly served on hosted pool.

sam (runtime): quick impact assessment: ~1.8k requests hit hosted pool, from ~14:47 to 15:05 UTC. ~430 responses had mismatched model variants (gptx-8q -> gptx-4q fallback) and ~70 requests retried/failed. No data exfil seen in logs but need for audit.

tina (customer-svcs): notifying acme-corp; sharing estimated impact and mitigation performed. They asked whether any PII might have been exposed — need security/eng to confirm.

maya (eng-sre): security check: logs show only model inference requests and tenant-id headers; hosted pool writes are segregated but policies assume no cross-tenant KV leakage. I'll tag eng-security for a deeper audit.

alex_m (oncall): eng-security: @jamie_sec pls triage for audit: check storage access logs and ensure no KV access across tenant boundaries during spillover window (14:47-15:05 UTC).

devops-bot: patch rolled to infra-ci templating: add guardrail to ensure fallback_order contains 'dedicated' for tenants with reserved capacity. CI run queued.

maya (eng-sre): next actions: 1) keep route override for 1h, then canonical policy validated before removing 2) add a fast alert for policy-generation anomalies (missing tiers) 3) run canary sweep to ensure template doesn't regress other tenants.

sam (runtime): I'll run a model-output regression on the 430 mismatched outputs and flag any quality backsliding to Product.

tina (customer-svcs): updating acme-corp with timeline and mitigation. They want an incident follow-up with RCA and mitigations.

alex_m (oncall): handing off to maya for postmortem and to coordinate RCA write-up. I'll stay on until security confirms no exposure. If anything spikes, page me immediately.

maya (eng-sre): acknowledged. I'll produce a follow-up doc with timeline, diff of config change, mitigation commands, and recommended guardrails.

sam (runtime): tagging notes for follow-up: - autoscaler logs for dedicated-acme-1 14:30-15:10 - routing decision traces for every acme-corp request in window - model-variant assignment logs - KV-cache persistency checks

alex_m (oncall): closing out the realtime page. Incident moved to 'mitigated'. Will transition to 'postmortem' channel after security sign-off. Great work, team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity=P0, incident_id=INC-20231234, responders=[alex_m,maya,sam,tina], followup=RCA required.
